content: The great flaw of penetration is not that it fails to reach the point, but that it goes past it.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In François de La Rochefoucauld's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
